caption: Mark deliberately connects Jesus’s death with Psalm 22. But extreme agony is a broad human experience, not a specific prediction of Calvary.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did Psalm 22 predict Calvary’s agony? The psalm describes a body failing near death. Mark describes Jesus crying out and dying on the cross.
slides.body: The psalm describes a body failing near death. Mark describes Jesus crying out and dying on the cross.
slides.heading: Did Psalm 22 predict Calvary’s agony?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Ps 22:14-15: My strength is dried up … You lay me in the dust of death.
slides.body: My strength is dried up … You lay me in the dust of death.
slides.heading: Ps 22:14-15

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Mk 15:34–37, BSB: Jesus cried out, ‘My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?’ … Then He breathed His last.
slides.body: Jesus cried out, ‘My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?’ … Then He breathed His last.
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Mk 15:34–37

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Mark makes a real connection Jesus quotes the opening of Psalm 22. Readers are clearly meant to see his death through this ancient lament.
slides.body: Jesus quotes the opening of Psalm 22. Readers are clearly meant to see his death through this ancient lament.
slides.heading: Mark makes a real connection

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But agony is not very specific Many people suffer terribly before death. The psalm fits Jesus, but it does not uniquely predict Calvary.
slides.body: Many people suffer terribly before death. The psalm fits Jesus, but it does not uniquely predict Calvary.

title: Agony at Calvary
